origin.description: The printed width of each element.
origin.usage: utf8_width(x, encode = TRUE, quote = FALSE, utf8 = NULL)

arguments.name: encode
arguments.text: Measure the escaped form. Controls then have a width.

arguments.name: quote
arguments.text: Add two for the surrounding quotes, and escape internal quotes.

arguments.name: utf8
arguments.text: When false, a non-ASCII string is missing unless encode is true.

origin.details: Emoji and wide characters count as two. Combining marks and default ignorables count as zero.
origin.value: An integer width, or None when the text cannot be printed.

translation.description: Widths come from the utf8 1.2.6 character table. None is R's NA.

arguments.name: encode
arguments.text: Measure the escaped form. Controls then have a width.

arguments.name: quote
arguments.text: Add two for the surrounding quotes, and escape internal quotes.

arguments.name: utf8
arguments.text: When false, a non-ASCII string is missing unless encode is true.

translation.details: encode false returns None for a control. quote true makes a quotation mark width 4.
translation.value: An integer width, or None when the text cannot be printed.
translation.example:
from utf8 import utf8_width
print(" ".join(str(item) for item in utf8_width(["fa\u00e7ile", "\U0001F600", "\u4e16", "e\u0301"])))
